title: Understanding Bias in Estimators
text: Bias in an estimator refers to the difference between the expected value of the estimator and the true value of the parameter being estimated. Consider how increasing the number of observations might affect this difference.

title: Effect of More Observations
text: When you increase the number of observations, you generally get a better estimate of the true parameter. Think about how this might affect the bias of the estimator.

title: Comparing One Roll to $$100$$ Rolls
text: Consider the difference in the maximum outcome when rolling a die once versus rolling it $$100$$ times. How does this affect the bias?
